Title: ALAKARIA
Date: 3-Mar-24
Content:  Saudi Real Estate Co. has published its 2023 financial results, revealing a decline in sales/revenue and net profit compared to the preceding year. The company reported sales/revenue of SAR 1,814.2 million in 2023, representing an 11.56% decrease from SAR 2,051.3 million in 2022. Net profit for 2023 stood at SAR 67.6 million, a 38.82% decrease from SAR 110.5 million in 2022.

        The decline in revenue can be attributed to several factors, including a SAR 531 million decrease in unit sales revenue due to the recording of the Dahia project sales in the previous year, a SAR 59 million decrease in land plot sales revenue primarily due to the sale of Qurtoba land in the previous year and reduced Akaria Park sales in the current year, and a SAR 31 mi

Title: SPM
Date: 5-Mar-24
Content: The Saudi Paper Manufacturing Company has announced the signing of a non-binding understanding agreement with TOSCOTEC, a leading global paper machine manufacturer based in Italy. The agreement covers the supply of a new production line, specifically designed to produce sanitary paper rolls with a capacity of 60,000 tons annually. This addition will bring the company's total production capacity to 250,000 tons per year.
The primary objectives of this agreement are to expand the company's market share, support national exports to the Middle East, Europe, and Africa, and align with the Kingdom's Vision 2030. Title: AZM
Date: 5-Mar-24
Content: Saudi AZM for Communication and Information Technology Co. announced its board of directors' recommendation to the extraordinary general assembly to buy up to 1,000,000 ordinary shares, valued at 20,000,000 Saudi riyals, for retention as treasury shares. These shares will be allocated to employees under the company's stock program. The acquisition will be financed through internal resources, and the purchased shares will not possess voting rights in general assembly meetings. The board's decision was made on March 5, 2024, and requires approval from the extraordinary general assembly, along with meeting financial solvency requirements as per the Companies Law.

Title: ALRAJHI
Date: 6-Mar-24
Content: Al Rajhi Bank has recently announced the completion of its offer of U.S. dollar denominated sustainable Sukuk under its international Sukuk program. The offer, worth USD 1 billion, consists of 5,000 Sukuk with a par value of USD 200,000 and a return of 5.047% per annum. The Sukuk will mature in 5 years, with the option for early redemption in specific cases as outlined in the offering circular. The Sukuk will be listed on the London Stock Exchange's International Securities Market and can be sold under Regulation S of the US Securities Act of 1933, as amended.

Date: 6-Mar-24
Content:  Saudi Electricity Company has published its audited annual consolidated financial results for the fiscal year ending 31-12-2023. The report indicates a 4.51% growth in sales/revenue, reaching 75,330 million Saudi Arabia Riyals compared to 72,079 million Saudi Arabia Riyals in 2022. However, the net profit saw a significant decrease of 32.28%, dropping to 10,249 million Saudi Arabia Riyals from 15,135 million Saudi Arabia Riyals in 2022.

        The gross profit and operational profit also experienced declines of 21.45% and 21.24%, respectively. The decrease in net profit can be attributed to several factors, including higher operating and maintenance costs due to growing business and operating assets, increasing maintenance programs, and h

Additionally, financing costs rose due to the high-interest rate environment and increased funding obtained during the current year for capital projects. Title: ATHEEB TELECOM
Date: 6-Mar-24
Content: Etihad Atheeb Telecommunications Co. (GO) has announced the signing of a memorandum of understanding with Aramco Digital Co. The MoU focuses on collaborative efforts in open RAN deployment for 5G and private 5G industrial use cases, aiming to strengthen the relationship between the two entities and elevate it to higher levels. Title: AWPT
Date: 24-Mar-24
Content: Alkhorayef Water and Power Technologies Co. has announced the successful financial closing of the Independent Water Transmission Pipeline (IWTP) Build, Operate and Transfer (BOT) project. The project, valued at 8.4 billion SAR, involves a capital expenditure of 2.4 billion SAR and a 35-year duration. The Rayis – Rabigh IWTP is the first project in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to be developed under a BOT model.
The project aims to provide Makkah and Madinah regions with drinking water, featuring a transmission capacity of 500,000 m3/day and a length of 150 km. Construction for the project is set to begin and is expected to be completed within a 30-month timeframe. The commercial operation date (SPCOD) is scheduled for Q2 of 2026.

Title: NGDC
Date: 28-Mar-24
Content: NGDC has announced its financial results for the year ending on December 31, 2023. The company reported a 1.63% increase in sales/revenue, reaching 92,485 thousand Saudi Arabia Riyals, up from 91,005 thousand in the previous year. Gross profit saw a 10.14% increase, totaling 8,775 thousand compared to 7,967 thousand in 2022.

These companies have been carrying out securities business within the Kingdom without proper authorization from the CMA or qualifying as exempt persons under the Securities Business Regulations.

M3 expanded by 2.3%, primarily due to an increased M2, despite a 19.4 billion decline in government deposits.

Title: YSCC
Date: 30-Apr-24
Content: Yamama Cement Co. has published its financial results for the first quarter of 2024. The company recorded a 2.198% decrease in sales compared to Q1 2023, primarily due to lower sales volumes during Ramadan. However, gross profit, operational profit, and net profit all experienced growth.
The net profit saw a 2.344% increase compared to the same quarter last year, attributed to a decrease in the cost of sales and an increase in other revenues. Total comprehensive income also rose by 2.275%.
Compared to the previous quarter, sales increased by 21.893%, while net profit grew by 118.028%, driven by higher sales values and increased other revenues.

Title: ALMUNAJEM
Date: 30-Apr-24
Content: Almunajem Foods Co. has announced the signing of a binding share purchase agreement with substantial shareholders in Balady Poultry Trading Company on 29 April 2024. According to the agreement, Almunajem Foods Co. will purchase 1,511,100 shares, equivalent to 23% of Balady Company's shares, for a total value of SAR 181,332,000. The transaction remains subject to several pre-closing conditions and the approval of relevant authorities, including the General Authority for Competition. Upon completion, Almunajem Foods Co.'s ownership will represent 40% of Balady Company's total shares. The company plans to partially self-finance the transaction and partially fund it through external sources.

Title: CBUAE Maintains the Base Rate at 5.40% 
02 May 2024
Date: 2-May-24
Content: The Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE) has announced its decision to keep the Base Rate applicable to the Overnight Deposit Facility (ODF) steady at 5.40%. This choice was made in response to the US Federal Reserve's recent announcement to hold the Interest Rate on Reserve Balances (IORB) constant.
Additionally, CBUAE has decided to preserve the interest rate applicable to short-term liquidity borrowing from the CBUAE at 50 basis points above the Base Rate for all standing credit facilities.
The Base Rate, which is tied to the US Federal Reserve's IORB, serves as a barometer for the overall tone of monetary policy and establishes an effective lower limit for overnight money market interest rates within the UAE.

Title: SAUDI CABLE
Date: 19-May-24
Content: Saudi Cable Company has announced the termination of its legal consultation contract with Dr. Wael Bafaqih & Partners Company. The decision comes after the lawyer's request to obtain 18% of the company's shares by holding a special extraordinary general assembly to vote on increasing the capital, allegedly based on a prior agreement with the former CEO, Mr. Nael Fayez.
Upon reviewing the contract, the company's management discovered discrepancies regarding the percentage of shares to be granted to the lawyer. The initial agreement stipulated that the lawyer would receive 2.5% of the total claims of the creditors identified during the financial restructuring procedures, but the Commercial Court in Jeddah, Fourth Circuit, ruled that the FRP trustee

ructuring procedures, but the Commercial Court in Jeddah, Fourth Circuit, ruled that the FRP trustee, not the company's lawyer, was responsible for listing the creditors and submitting them to the court.

Content: Saudi Cement Company has announced that it will join the Industrial Sector Competitiveness Program, following a notification from Saudi Aramco to amend fuel prices used in the company's operations. The company had previously estimated a 13% increase in production costs due to the fuel price adjustment. However, after signing an agreement with the competitiveness program, the financial impact on the increase in the cost of production will be reduced to approximately 7%, starting from January 1, 2024. Date: 23-May-24
Content: The Capital Market Authority in Saudi Arabia has given its approval to KKR Saudi Limited to amend its Business Profile. Content: Saudi Cable Co. has announced the appointment of two new members to its Audit Committee: Mr. Hamza bin Ghulam Joharji and Mr. Saad bin Abdulmohsen Alhamidi. Title: The CBUAE successfully launches Project mBridge Minimum Viable Product platform for early adopters 
05 June 2024
Date: 5-Jun-24
Content:  The Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE) has successfully introduced the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) platform of the mBridge project, a multi-central bank digital currency (CBDC) platform for wholesale cross-border payments and settlement. Date: 10-Jun-24
Content: The Capital Markets Authority (CMA) has published a disclaimer notice on its webpage, highlighting that the information provided on the site should be used solely as a reference. The CMA cautions users that the information may not be complete, accurate, or up-to-date and encourages them to consult the official scanned documents linked on the page for reliable content. The CMA clarifies that they strive to maintain accurate information, but cannot guarantee its quality at any given time. The disclaimer serves to inform users that, in case of discrepancies between the webpage content and the attached official documents, the latter shall be considered authoritative.

Title: The UAE SFWG launches the Principles for Sustainability-Related Disclosures for Reporting Entities in line with the Year of Sustainability
Date: 10-Jun-24
Content: The UAE Sustainable Finance Working Group (SFWG), comprised of UAE authorities, has released the ‘Principles for Sustainability-Related Disclosures for Reporting Entities’. These principles outline the minimum expectations for sustainability-related disclosures, focusing on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors. The principles target reporting entities, urging them to establish adequate policies, procedures, and systems for disclosing sustainability-related matters.
